hook: A U.S. military operator's MISREP from the Arabian Gulf in 2020 records a brief, single-sentence UAP observation at 12:46Z, noting one probable UAP at a specific military grid coordinate with no impact on the ongoing mission.
why_it_matters: This document illustrates the minimalist nature of field-level UAP reporting: the entire substantive content is a single sentence in the GENTEXT section, with the operator's identity partially redacted and no sensor data, description of appearance, or follow-up action recorded. It demonstrates that UAP encounters were logged and routed through standard military reporting channels (MISREP to AARO) even when operationally inconsequential. The brevity and 'PROB' qualifier suggest the observer was uncertain whether the object was a true UAP.

key_findings.finding: A single probable UAP was observed at 12:46 Zulu time at a specific military grid location in the Arabian Gulf.

quotes.text: AT 1246Z, [RAB OBSERVED 1X PROB UAP IVO 3SKT4255899519. NO MISSION IMPACT, [QJ CONTINUED ORIGINAL TASKING.

key_findings.finding: The observer classified the object as a 'probable' UAP, not a confirmed one, indicating uncertainty at the time of observation.
The UAP had no impact on the mission and the operator continued their original tasking without interruption.

key_findings.finding: The observer's callsign or unit designation is redacted, and the report section is classified at the (6B) exemption level.

Six of the document's seven pages contain no extractable text, meaning all structured MISREP fields (time on target, coordinates in standard fields, sensor data, etc.) are either blank, redacted, or did not survive OCR extraction.
